questions.q: What does RACI stand for, and what does it map?
options: Report, Act, Close, Inform -- a four-step incident timeline
Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed -- a model mapping each decision or activity to specific people in those roles
Review, Approve, Confirm, Investigate -- a model used only for software releases
Risk, Analysis, Containment, Impact -- a scoring system for incident severity
questions.explain: RACI is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed, and it exists to remove ambiguity about who does what.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Responsible and Accountable in the RACI model?
options: Responsible always outranks Accountable in every decision
Accountable means being told about a decision after it's already made
Responsible is who does the work; Accountable is who owns the decision and answers for the outcome, and there should be exactly one Accountable person per item
Responsible and Accountable always refer to the exact same person
questions.explain: Collapsing these two distinct roles into one is exactly what causes conflicting action during a live incident.

questions.q: What is the Incident Commander's role on an IR team?
options: Handles customer-facing communications exclusively, with no decision authority
Only responsible for writing the after-action report once the incident is over
A role that exists only in ransomware incidents, not other scenario types
Holds overall decision authority for the incident and coordinates the team, usually Accountable for the incident as a whole
questions.explain: The IC makes the final call on major decisions and is typically the single Accountable party for the incident overall.

questions.q: In the "take a production system offline" example, why is Legal marked as Consulted rather than Accountable?
options: Legal is always the one who physically executes the isolation
Legal is only Informed after the decision has already been made
Legal gives input before the decision, since taking a system offline can affect evidence preservation or contractual obligations, but the Incident Commander owns the actual go/no-go call
Legal has no role in that decision at all
questions.explain: Consulted means giving input before the decision is made -- Legal flags the exposure, but the IC remains Accountable for the final call.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is ambiguity about who is Accountable during a live incident actively dangerous?
options: Multiple people may independently believe they have authority to make a major call and take conflicting action at the same time
It only matters for incidents that don't require any containment steps
It is purely a paperwork issue with no effect on the actual response
It has no real effect since every IR team member has identical authority by default
questions.explain: The production-system example shows exactly this: the technical lead and the CEO could give directly conflicting orders at the same moment.
